tagline: AI assistant for writing, reasoning, coding, and document work.
verdictSummary: A Claude-shaped wrapper — chat over the Anthropic API, document upload, saved project contexts — is genuinely easy to build. What stays out of reach is the model itself, its long-context quality, and Artifacts and Projects as a polished product surface rather than a plain API call.
coreLoopDIY: A chat app over the Anthropic API, with document upload, conversation history, and a lightweight 'project' grouping for shared context.
whatYouLose: the frontier model and its continuous upgrades
Artifacts as an interactive canvas, not just returned text
flat-rate pricing that doesn't punish heavy use
whyPeopleStillPay: The quality sits in the model and the product surface around it, not in the chat window — a wrapper gets you the same API, but none of Anthropic's product work on top of it.
notes: A 'no' that still leaves a genuinely usable, often cheaper wrapper for people who mainly chat and don't need Artifacts.
prompt:
Build a thin client on the Anthropic API: a chat interface with streaming replies, a conversation sidebar, and Markdown rendering. Let a conversation carry an editable system prompt, with Sonnet as the default model and the option to switch to a larger model per conversation. Add 'projects': a project groups related conversations and holds a handful of reference documents (plain text or PDF) that get prepended as context to every chat inside it — use the API's prompt caching on those documents so repeated context doesn't get re-billed every message. Store everything in a real database with full-text search across all conversations, and let any thread export to Markdown. Show a running cost estimate per conversation and per month from the API's usage data, so keeping this instead of paying a flat fee is a decision backed by a number, not a feeling.

Do not build Artifacts as an interactive canvas, the mobile apps, or flat-rate pricing for heavy use — if the cost meter shows genuinely heavy usage, a flat-rate plan wins on price, and the honest move is to switch back rather than keep optimizing around it.

faq.q: Can I import my Claude conversation history?
faq.a: Claude.ai lets you export your data, including conversations, and the export maps reasonably well onto this build's storage — a short one-off script converts the export format.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a responsive web page, yes, if it's hosted somewhere reachable. There's no native app and no offline mode.

faq.q: What does it actually cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting is a few dollars a month; token costs for light-to-medium chat use are often well under the flat subscription price, especially once prompt caching is wired up for repeated project context.

faq.q: What's the one thing that genuinely doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Artifacts as a real product surface. The API can return code or documents as text, but the interactive, versioned canvas Claude.ai renders them into is product work this wrapper doesn't replicate.
